submission:
How to Change Your Car's Engine Oil: A Step-by-Step Guide

Changing your own engine oil is one of the easiest ways to save money and extend the life of your vehicle. Before you begin, gather the following: a socket wrench, an oil filter wrench, a drain pan, a funnel, the correct grade of motor oil (check your owner's manual, often 5W-30 or 0W-20), and a new oil filter.

Step 1: Warm the engine for two to three minutes so the oil flows freely, then turn it off. Step 2: Raise the front of the car with a jack and secure it on jack stands. Never work under a car held up only by a jack. Step 3: Place the drain pan beneath the oil drain plug, then loosen the plug with your socket wrench and let the old oil drain completely. Step 4: Remove the old oil filter with the filter wrench, lightly oil the gasket of the new filter, and screw it on hand-tight. Step 5: Replace the drain plug and tighten it to the torque listed in your manual. Step 6: Using the funnel, add the recommended amount of fresh oil, then check the dipstick to confirm the correct level.

Always dispose of used motor oil responsibly at an auto-parts store or recycling center. Regular oil changes every 5,000 to 7,500 miles keep your engine clean and running smoothly for years to come.
